$comment: Agent surface registry. This is the ONLY place tool-specific paths/formats live.
If a tool changes its format, edit this file - never the installer code.
confidence: high = verified against the tool's own docs//behaviour at time of writing;
medium = widely documented but not re-verified; low = best-effort, please confirm.
root-pointer   -> a small markdown file at repo root pointing at .agent-toolkit/CORE.md
dir-rules-md   -> one .md file inside a rules directory
dir-rules-mdc  -> one .mdc file (YAML frontmatter) inside a rules directory
surfaces.skills.mode: link = symlink to .agent-toolkit/skills (no duplication), null = unsupported
surfaces.mcp.scope: project = we can write it, global = user must configure manually (we emit instructions)
surfaces.hooks: how a tool registers a SessionStart hook. Only declared for agents that actually support one; the session-reminder pack fills it in.

shared_files.AGENTS.md: Written once when any agent that consumes it is selected.

agents.name: Claude Code
agents.notes: Only agent with native progressive-disclosure skills, slash commands and subagents. SessionStart hooks let the toolkit put its rules in context every session.

agents.name: Cursor
agents.notes: MDC frontmatter supports description/globs/alwaysApply. Glob-scoped rules are the closest thing to skills outside Claude Code.

agents.name: OpenAI Codex CLI
agents.notes: MCP is configured globally in TOML, not per project. Installer emits manual setup instructions instead of writing it.

agents.name: GitHub Copilot / VS Code
agents.notes: Verified against VS Code docs. MCP uses the key 'servers' (not mcpServers) in .vscode/mcp.json; 'type' is required for remote HTTP servers only. VS Code also reads AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md, plus .github/instructions/*.instructions.md with an applyTo glob.

agents.name: Gemini CLI
agents.notes: Verified against the gemini-cli source docs: project settings at ./.gemini/settings.json, MCP under the top-level mcpServers key, context file GEMINI.md.

agents.name: Windsurf
agents.notes: Windsurf is now Devin. Current docs prefer .devin/rules/*.md, but .windsurf/rules/*.md is still read for backward compatibility - which is why it is used here: it works on both old and new versions. The legacy .windsurfrules file is also still read, and AGENTS.md is fully supported. Switch the path to .devin/rules if you only target current versions.

agents.name: Cline
agents.notes: Verified: workspace rules live in the .clinerules/ DIRECTORY (all .md/.txt files are combined). Cline also reads AGENTS.md. MCP is stored in extension state, not the project, so it is left to manual setup.

agents.name: Roo Code
agents.notes: Verified: .roo/rules/ is the primary directory form (.roorules is the legacy fallback); files are read recursively in alphabetical order. Roo also auto-loads AGENTS.md unless roo-cline.useAgentRules is false. The .roo/mcp.json path is not covered by the rules documentation - verify before relying on it.

agents.name: JetBrains Junie
agents.notes: CORRECTED: Junie now reads AGENTS.md from the project root as the primary guidelines file; .junie/guidelines.md is the legacy format (still supported). Junie also combines .junie/playbook.md and .junie/rules/*.md when present. MCP is configured through the IDE, not a project file.

agents.name: OpenCode
agents.notes: Verified against opencode.ai docs: AGENTS.md at the project root, config in opencode.json under the top-level 'mcp' key. Local servers take {type:'local', command:[bin, ...args], enabled:true}; remote take {type:'remote', url, enabled:true}.

agents.name: Aider
agents.notes: CORRECTED: CONVENTIONS.md is only a naming convention - Aider does NOT read it automatically. It must be loaded with `aider --read CONVENTIONS.md` or a `read:` entry in .aider.conf.yml, which the installer now writes. Aider does not auto-read AGENTS.md either, and has no MCP support.

agents.name: Amp
agents.notes: Verified: Amp reads AGENTS.md (and AGENT.md) from the nearest directory upward, so the project root file applies everywhere. MCP is configured outside the project.

agents.name: Zed
agents.notes: Verified against Zed docs: .rules is checked FIRST in its precedence list, ahead of AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md, so writing .rules reliably wins. MCP servers are called 'context servers' and are configured outside the project.

agents.name: Kilo Code
agents.notes: Kilo now prefers .kilo/rules/ configured via kilo.jsonc, but .kilocode/rules/ remains supported for backward compatibility and is used here so the same file works across versions. Verify .kilocode/mcp.json against your version.
